per_claim.source_quote: On this task an integer read off the declared target structure -- free wherever a target is declared, and undefined where one is not -- matches a transformer trained on roughly two million chemical-mapping profiles (+0.3225 against +0.3295, difference [-0.0737, +0.0866]). Holding it fixed, both predictors retain a real but modest ordering ability (+0.2380 and +0.1820, both $p<0.001$), worth 1.96 points of recovery when used to break the baseline's ties. The advantage has a measured domain: it is +0.3339 on the 3{,}406 interventions whose pair the probing data confirms and +0.1115 on the 635 it does not, where no interval separates any predictor from it. Any claim that a structure predictor knows which mutations rescue must be stated as an increment over helix depth, and to our knowledge none has been.

per_claim.source_quote: Across 4 independent implementations and three budgets -- and a fifth, the only pseudoknot-capable one, added because this corpus is a pseudoknot round and losing at every budget (+0.1321 against +0.1613 at the tightest) -- no model outperforms a free integer as a standalone ranker of which interventions to build: none of 12 intervals excludes zero, and against a margin fixed as the gain one extra construct buys ($delta=+0.0473$), 9 are equivalent to free depth while the remaining 3 fail on the side of being worse. The panel's largest structure-agreement margin, +0.260, converts to 1.0% of this corpus's rescuing interventions, and at the tightest budget its sign inverts (-0.0159 [-0.0278, -0.0036]) -- a measured crossing rather than three points: swept over 19 budgets the gap changes sign exactly 1 time, at 15.0%--17.5% of a design built, surviving any dropped target, 4 of 5 rescue thresholds, and 5 of 6 predictor pairs -- the only pair that does not invert being two implementations of one model family. A structure-benchmark margin is an average, and the better a model ranks on that average the further from the top of its own list its advantage lies. A budgeted experimenter only ever sees the top.

per_claim.source_quote: Three families produce the pairing probabilities this paper scores, and the boundary between the first two is where its result falls. Thermodynamic models minimise or sum a free energy over a nearest-neighbour decomposition of the structure zuker1981optimal,mccaskill1990equilibrium, hofacker1994fast,lorenz2011vienna, with parameters measured by optical melting on short duplexes, coaxial stacks and helix ends freier1986improved,walter1994coaxial,serra1995predicting, xia1998thermodynamic,mathews1999expanded,turner2010nndb. Learned-parameter models keep that decomposition, or a close relative, and fit its weights discriminatively to structural data instead do2006contrafold,andronescu2007efficient,waymentsteele2022rna; the statistical basis for doing so on probing data is developed separately waymentsteele2021theoretical. Neural models drop the decomposition and predict pairing from sequence with a learned architecture and no explicit energy singh2019spotrna,sato2021rna,fu2022ufold, ribonanzanet2024.
